summary: Spiral galaxies, like the Milky Way, transform at some point in time into a rotationally supported system. Using an extant data-set consisting of 319 835 sub-giants from LAMOST with precise ages from the literature, we determine, for the first time the age when the Milky Way disk spins up, i.e. when the mean circular velocity changes from halo-like to disk-like. We find in concordance previous studies that the spin-up takes place for -1.25 < [Fe/H] <- 0.9 and we can date this transition to a mean age of 12.1 +/- 2.8 Gyr (median age 12.4 Gyr). We further study when the disk became rotationally supported, i.e. when the ordered, disky motion dominates over the random motions. We find that this happens for $-1.25<$[Fe/H]$<-1$. The transition is very rapid in age. This gives support to that the spin-up seen in this and other works genuinely traces the motion to a rotationally supported disk, which has not previously been shown. These transitions are traced by the high-alpha stars. while the low-alpha stars do not spin-up but start directly at approximately the circular velocity seen for the Sun today. The low-alpha disk is rotationally supported with no transition period in [Fe/H] or in age.

AI.tldr: Using 319,835 LAMOST sub-giants with precise ages, the study dates the Milky Way disk spin-up (transition from halo-like to disk-like circular velocity) to a mean age of 12.1±2.8 Gyr, occurring at [Fe/H] between -1.25 and -0.9, and finds the disk becomes rotationally supported at [Fe/H] between -1.25 and -1 with a rapid age transition. High-alpha stars trace these transitions, while low-alpha stars show no spin-up, starting directly at near-Solar circular velocity.
AI.motivation: To determine when the Milky Way disk spins up and becomes rotationally supported, and to date these transitions using precise stellar ages from a large sub-giant sample.
AI.method: Analysis of 319,835 sub-giants from LAMOST with literature-derived precise ages; measurement of mean circular velocity changes as a function of [Fe/H] and age to identify the spin-up epoch and rotational support transition.
AI.result: Spin-up occurs at [Fe/H] between -1.25 and -0.9 with mean age 12.1±2.8 Gyr (median 12.4 Gyr). Rotational support transition occurs at [Fe/H] between -1.25 and -1, with rapid age transition. High-alpha stars trace these transitions; low-alpha stars show no spin-up and start at near-Solar circular velocity.
AI.conclusion: The spin-up genuinely traces the transition to a rotationally supported disk, supported by the rapid age transition. The low-alpha disk is rotationally supported throughout with no transition period.

title: B-Fields and Star Formation across Scales with TRAO (B-FROST): CO Abundances, Dynamics and Relative Orientations in the Translucent High Latitude Cloud MBM12
comment: 21 pages, 16 figures, accepted in Astronomy and Astrophysics
summary: In our Galaxy, the average star formation efficiency is of the order of a few percent. We investigated the high-latitude molecular cloud MBM12 as part of the B-fields and star formation across scales (B-FROST) survey with the Taeduk Radio Astronomical Observatory (TRAO) to assess why star formation activity in MBM12 is low. We combine {\it Herschel}-based, locally $κ_ν$-calibrated $N$(H$_2$) estimates with $^{12}$CO and $^{13}$CO ($J=1-0$) observations (2.5$^\circ \times$3$^\circ$ at 48$''$) to map $N$(CO), $X$(CO), and [CO/H$_2$], compute multi-scale $α_{\rm vir}$ and mass-size scaling laws from dendrograms, and derive the histogram of relative orientations from {\it Planck} dust polarisation. We identify four main regions based on velocities that have H$_2$ column densities ranging from $2\times10^{20}$ cm$^{-2} - 1.3\times10^{22}$ cm$^{-2}$. The average $X$(CO) is close to the galactic average, with variations below $X_{\rm Gal}$ from collisional de-excitation in low-density gas, and above $X_{\rm Gal}$ from CO photodissociation at cloud edges. The hierarchical structures follow a broken power law mass-size relation $M=AR^α$. The values of $α_{\rm vir}$ ranged from $3-60$, with the smallest values at 0.1 pc scales. The mass-size relations for the structures with the lowest $α_{\rm vir}$ have scaling factors $A$ three times larger than those of high $α_{\rm vir}$ structures, indicating external pressure one order of magnitude larger. We found a transition of parallel to perpendicular between column density structures and magnetic field orientations at $N$(H$_2$) $= 4.5 \times 10^{21}$ cm$^{-2}$. We provide the first integrated chemical, dynamical, and magnetic field analysis of MBM12. Scale-dependent mass-size and virial analysis can further constrain the role of external pressure in regulating the star formation efficiency.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the high-latitude molecular cloud MBM12 using multi-wavelength observations (Herschel, TRAO CO lines, Planck dust polarization) to understand its low star formation efficiency (~few %). The study finds that MBM12 is characterized by high virial parameters (α_vir=3-60), external pressure playing a key role in regulating structures, and a transition from parallel to perpendicular alignment between column density structures and magnetic fields at N(H₂)=4.5×10²¹ cm⁻².
AI.motivation: To understand why the star formation efficiency in the high-latitude molecular cloud MBM12 is low, given that the average Galactic star formation efficiency is only a few percent.
AI.method: Combined Herschel-based, locally κ_ν-calibrated N(H₂) estimates with ¹²CO and ¹³CO (J=1-0) observations from TRAO (2.5°×3° at 48″), mapped N(CO), X(CO), and [CO/H₂], computed multi-scale α_vir and mass-size scaling laws from dendrograms, and derived histograms of relative orientations from Planck dust polarization.
AI.result: Four main velocity regions identified with N(H₂) range 2×10²⁰–1.3×10²² cm⁻². Average X(CO) close to galactic average. Hierarchical structures follow broken power-law mass-size relation M=AR^α. α_vir ranges 3–60, lowest at 0.1 pc scales. Low-α_vir structures have 3× larger scaling factor A, indicating 10× larger external pressure. Transition from parallel to perpendicular alignment at N(H₂)=4.5×10²¹ cm⁻².
AI.conclusion: This is the first integrated chemical, dynamical, and magnetic field analysis of MBM12. Scale-dependent mass-size and virial analysis can further constrain the role of external pressure in regulating star formation efficiency in this cloud.

title: Euclid: Early Release Observations -- The formation of peanutty dwarf galaxies in Perseus
comment: 21 pages, 18 figures, 5 tables. Submitted to A&A
summary: Dwarf galaxies in dense cluster environments are susceptible to tidal interactions that can alter their morphology and kinematics. Boxy isophotes are well studied in massive galaxies but remain poorly understood in dwarfs. We aim to identify and characterise boxy/peanutty dwarf galaxies in the Perseus cluster and determine the origin of their isophotal shapes. Using Euclid Early Release Observations of the Perseus cluster, we present a cumulative light fraction method for robustly measuring the isophotal shape parameter $c_4$, particularly suited to low surface brightness regimes. From ~1100 cataloged dwarfs, we select a clean sample of ~190 early-type systems with reliable $c_4$ measurement. Observed trends are interpreted through comparison with mock Euclid observations of $N$-body simulations of tidally transformed dwarfs. We identify 13 dwarfs with significantly boxy isophotes ($c_4 < -0.0175$). These galaxies lack visible thin disks, lie on the cluster red sequence, and show no preferential spatial concentration within Perseus. We find a significant anticorrelation between $c_4$ and effective radius: larger galaxies exhibit more boxy isophotes. An analogous size-shape anticorrelation is recovered in the simulations, where inner regions are dominated by box orbits associated with a triaxial peanut structure and outer regions by short-axis tube orbits. The boxy dwarfs in Perseus are tidally transformed remnants of moderately rotating progenitors, with boxy isophotes tracing inner box-orbit-dominated peanut structures. The size-shape correlation arises from viewing geometry: face-on orientations reveal the rectangular profile of the elongated triaxial structure (large and boxy), while edge-on views yield rounder, compact morphologies. Our sample represents an orientation-selected subset of tidally transformed, peanutty dwarfs in the cluster.

AI.tldr: Using Euclid observations of the Perseus cluster, we identify 13 boxy/peanutty dwarf galaxies and show their isophotal shapes arise from tidal transformation of moderately rotating progenitors, with a size-shape anticorrelation explained by viewing geometry of triaxial peanut structures.
AI.motivation: Boxy isophotes are well studied in massive galaxies but remain poorly understood in dwarf galaxies, particularly in dense cluster environments where tidal interactions are prevalent.
AI.method: Applied a cumulative light fraction method to measure the isophotal shape parameter c4 from Euclid Early Release Observations of the Perseus cluster, selecting ~190 clean early-type dwarfs from ~1100 cataloged systems, and compared observed trends with mock Euclid observations of N-body simulations of tidally transformed dwarfs.
AI.result: Identified 13 dwarfs with significantly boxy isophotes (c4 < -0.0175) that lack thin disks, lie on the cluster red sequence, and show no spatial concentration. Found a significant anticorrelation between c4 and effective radius, recovered in simulations where inner regions are dominated by box orbits from triaxial peanut structures and outer regions by short-axis tube orbits.
AI.conclusion: Boxy dwarfs in Perseus are tidally transformed remnants of moderately rotating progenitors; the size-shape correlation arises from viewing geometry (face-on reveals elongated triaxial structures as large and boxy, edge-on yields rounder compact morphologies), making the sample an orientation-selected subset of tidally transformed peanutty dwarfs.
